pr_title: TST: Added a test for groupby.prod
pr_body:
- [x] Closes #46573 

- The bug related to issue #46573  has been fixed in the current version.

- Added a test related to this issue. The test is designed to check if `groupby.prod` returns the same results as `prod`.

issue_context.title: BUG: prod and groupby.prod behave differently
issue_context.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the main branch of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame(
    data=[
        [5,	2, 17, 11, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 41, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 17, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 37, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 7, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 29, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 31, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 2, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 3, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 43, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 5, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 47, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 19, 7, 2, 3],
        [5,	2, 17, 23, 7, 2, 3],

    ],
    columns=['A','B','C','D','E','F','G']
)

df.prod()
#A            6103515625
#B                 16384
#C    168377826559400929
#D     47299214045268570 <-- correct value
#E          678223072849
#F                 16384
#G               4782969
#dtype: int64

df.groupby(['A','B','C','E','F','G']).prod()

#						D
#A	B	C	E	F	G	
#5	2	17	7	2	3	47299214045268568 <-- wrong value
```


### Issue Description

During a project that uses pandas groupby prod method I noticed possible bug.

The reproducible example should be clear but the core issue is that is seems that pandas prod() method behaves different
than pandas groupby prod method. The result is inconsistent. In the example, please inspect column "D"

### Expected Behavior

Correct output of column D during the groupby operation

### Installed Versions

<details>

'1.4.1'

</details>
comments:
@tf401
I have simplified your example a bit and discovered even weirder behavior: 
```
import pandas as pd
print("pd version:", pd.__version__)

def factory(i):
    return pd.DataFrame(
        data=[
            [1, 11],
            [1, 41],
            [1, 17],
            [1, 37],
            [1, 7],
            [1, 29],
            [1, 31],
            [1, 2],
            [1, 3],
            [1, 43],
            [1, 5],
            [1, 47],
            [1, 19],  # up to this line everything is fine
            [1, i],  # this line triggers the bug
        ],
        columns=["a", "b"],
        dtype="int64",
    )


for i in range(90):
    df = factory(i)
    df_prod = df.prod()["b"]
    df_groupby_prod = df.groupby(["a"]).prod().iloc[0, 0]
    diff = df_prod - df_groupby_prod
    if diff != 0:
        print(
            f"i={i}, diff={diff}, df_prod={df_prod}, df_groupby_prod={df_groupby_prod} "
        )
#sample output:
#pd version: 1.4.1
#i=9, diff=-2, df_prod=18508388104670310, df_groupby_prod=18508388104670312 
#i=11, diff=2, df_prod=22621363239041490, df_groupby_prod=22621363239041488 
#i=13, diff=-2, df_prod=26734338373412670, df_groupby_prod=26734338373412672 
#i=15, diff=2, df_prod=30847313507783850, df_groupby_prod=30847313507783848 
#i=17, diff=-2, df_prod=34960288642155030, df_groupby_prod=34960288642155032 
#...
#i=23, diff=2, df_prod=47299214045268570, df_groupby_prod=47299214045268568 
#...
#i=84, diff=-8, df_prod=172744955643589560, df_groupby_prod=172744955643589568 
#i=85, diff=14, df_prod=174801443210775150, df_groupby_prod=174801443210775136 
#i=86, diff=4, df_prod=176857930777960740, df_groupby_prod=176857930777960736 
#i=87, diff=-6, df_prod=178914418345146330, df_groupby_prod=178914418345146336 
#i=88, diff=16, df_prod=180970905912331920, df_groupby_prod=180970905912331904 
#i=89, diff=6, df_prod=183027393479517510, df_groupby_prod=183027393479517504 
```
Remarkably,  the difference is always a multiple of 2. 
The calculated values are also well below max np.int64 of 9_223_372_036_854_775_807, so probably no simple overflow error!

Found the bugging part! The groupby operation `prod` calculates correctly with dtype ```float64```, but before returning lands in pandas/core/dtypes/cast.py in function ```maybe_downcast_numeric``` where the call to ```astype``` lands in pandas/core/arrays/base.py. Here the resulting numpy cast is failing:
```
df=factory(23) #to replicate the OP example
df.groupby(["a"]).prod() #calling code 
```
![Capture](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/100441021/160921263-cda7e4ef-6495-4c70-abf6-e55e0969c7b2.PNG)
![bugging part](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/100441021/160922263-2b5535f6-71db-420c-af36-bdf7254a0fbf.PNG)

Minimal reproducing example is: 
```
import numpy as np
np.array(4.729921404526857e16, dtype="float64").astype("int64")
#array(47299214045268568, dtype=int64)
```
numpy version: '1.22.3'

Edit: 
seems to be a weird numpy thing! Floating point deviations from the real world are expected somewhere beyond >1e15, but why is the debugger able to display the true value...
```
np.array(4.729921404526857e16, dtype="float64").astype("int64") - np.array(47299214045268570, dtype="int64")
# -2
np.array(4.729921404526857e16, dtype="float64") - np.array(47299214045268570, dtype="int64")
# 0
np.array(4.729921404526857e16, dtype="float64") - np.array(47299214045268570, dtype="int64").astype('float')
# 0
```

Edit 2: the ```trans``` call in image 1 is not the problem!

@tf401 
Although not resolving the issue, hopefully it helped a bit! The explanations is probably found somewhere in numpy's exact representation of doubles and casting rules! Will do a quick check tomorrow and maybe it can be circumvented somehow in pandas ```astype``` cast, which is essentially a numpy cast to the target format! Somewhere in the ```groupby prod``` call the datatype changes to ```float64``` and that was unexpected! Will investigate further...

The standard ```prod``` call delegates directly (except for a gazilion sanity checks:) to the numpy ```prod``` method without anything in between and returns the result (and again with additional checks) : 
![pandas-issue-46573-pandas-core-nanops-py](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/100441021/161096839-c0d35dfa-c5cc-4e14-bb95-1979c00eb8d6.PNG)
![pandas-issue-46573-pandas-core-nanops-py-2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/100441021/161096872-bd01a8ab-a8fb-411f-8dfd-743059cad7cb.PNG)
 In the ```groupby prod``` this is done in the ```Grouper class``` with a pandas build in cython method and somewhere the ```dtype``` is changing to ```float64``` and the final numpy cast to the target ```dtype``` fails as shown above! By the way, the pandas ```astype``` does essentially nothing more than returning ```np.array(values,dtype=dtype)``` 

Edit: To mitigate this problem in the short term, you could use something like a c-style macro 
```
def LARGE_EQUALS(x, y):
    return abs(x - y) < YOUR_THRESHOLD
```
for huge values. Obviously it all depends on your exact usecase and is a bit dirty...

Just wanted to add: my suspicion is that the underlying c function ```prod``` in ```groupby``` has a signature like ```double(double[])``` and the final 'downcast' cannot be avoided at the moment. If so I will try to find a way to intercept this call for ```int64``` groups and instead use the numpy ```prod``` implementation, which can deal with these large integers. Might take a while though...
I now get the correct result on main. Could use a test in `tests/groupby/test_reductions.py`.
